defendants_label: Long Moua (CDCR Parole Agent, Badge #7472 — received BNN's file on or about Jan. 26, 2026, ~14 days after BNN filed the Derrick FAC; fabricated March 31, 2026 telehealth 'failure to attend treatment' violation by withholding the access code then submitting BNN's non-attendance as willful; authored Nov. 14, 2025 CDCR Form 1502-DR (Discharge Review Report), reviewed/e-signed by Noguchi, judicially questioned by Sacramento County Superior Court; ordered retaliatory transfer to Santa Clara GPS Unit on Jun. 29, 2026, 7 days after BNN served CDCR in separate lawsuit, citing 'too many violations'); and DOES 1–10, inclusive. NOTE: an earlier complaint draft named Gary Noguchi (CDCR Parole Agent, Badge #7284, Unit Supervisor San Joaquin County Parole GPS Unit — Moua's direct supervisor; co-defendant in Newanforbi v. Andrew Derrick et al. FAC, Case 2:26-cv-00004-DJC-JDP; co-authored the 1502-DR with Moua) and Joseelyn Rojo (CDCR Parole official) as co-defendants, and both were served under that draft (Noguchi Jul. 7, 2026; Rojo Jul. 14, 2026). Plaintiff has confirmed the narrowing to Moua-only in the operative Complaint v9 was a deliberate strategic choice, not an oversight — the claim against Moua is pleaded on its own facts, with Noguchi and Rojo reserved for potential later amendment as DOE defendants if discovery substantiates their supervisory involvement. FLAGGED RISK FOR THAT RESERVATION: Matter 3's July 24, 2026 order already dismissed a supervisory-liability theory against this same Noguchi 'for lack of supervisory-liability allegations under Hansen v. Black' (with leave to amend, not a final merits adjudication — and in the same order the court itself noted this sits in tension with Plaintiff's own July 22, 2026 self-executing voluntary dismissal of Noguchi from that action). Neither ruling forecloses a differently-pleaded supervisory theory here, but any future DOE amendment naming Noguchi should address Hansen v. Black head-on rather than repeat the pleading gap Matter 3 already identified. This matter also does not currently disclose its overlap with the discharge-review cluster (Matters 9, 10, 11, 15, 19) — Moua co-authored the same Nov. 14, 2025 Form 1502-DR whose facial defects are the entire subject of that cluster (see Matter 19, now the sole still-pending vehicle for that challenge). Separately, this matter's causal account of the June 29, 2026 retaliatory transfer (Moua's personal decision, driven by the fabricated telehealth violation) differs from Matters 3 and 15's account of the same transfer (institutional retaliation by 'Stockton parole,' Noguchi's unit, tied to the Matter 15 filing) — the two framings aren't mutually exclusive, but neither cross-references the other, and a factfinder crediting one causal story could undercut the other.
